name: pinned-replay
title: Pinned replay
description: The scroll-pinned run walkthrough from humanish.dev: a tall track pins a step rail and stage; scroll advances discrete panels (brief, lanes, evidence ledger, verify terminal) with an idle-snap that centers the nearest step. Below 1024px — or without JavaScript — panels stack as a readable list. Ships the Excalidraw study's metadata as demo data; the screenshots are not included, so point LANES[].img at your own captures. Excalidraw is the application studied in the demo data; it is not a Humanish adopter or endorser.
docs: Import all three stylesheets in your global CSS: @import "../styles/humanish/pinned-replay.css"; @import "../styles/humanish/persona-lane.css"; @import "../styles/humanish/terminal-cast.css";. The pinned desktop layout is gated on a "js" class on <html>; the component adds it on mount, and for a flash-free first paint you can also add it pre-paint: <script>document.documentElement.classList.add("js")</script> in <head>. The demo data constants (BRIEF_YAML, RAIL_ITEMS, LANES, VERIFY_CAST) are yours to replace; the scroll engine reads panels from the DOM, so add or remove panels freely. BRIEF_YAML is injected as HTML for its token spans — keep it a literal, never interpolate untrusted text. Respects prefers-reduced-motion.
